name: answer-quality-generic-smoke-v1
description: A small GENERIC general-knowledge question set authored for this harness. Its ONLY purpose is to prove the end-to-end pipeline + LLM-as-a-judge wiring runs (turn -> answer -> graded). It is NOT a measure of any adopter's real answer quality. Some questions carry context_docs (short, self-authored, public-domain facts) so the faithfulness/hallucination axes are exercised; some carry ideal_answer so the correctness axis compares against a target. Generic != your domain: copy testdata/domain.example.json and run this harness on your OWN Q&A for numbers that mean anything.

questions.question: What is the capital of France?

context_docs.text: France is a country in Western Europe. Its capital and largest city is Paris.

questions.question: At what temperature does water boil at sea level, in Celsius?

context_docs.text: At standard atmospheric pressure (sea level), pure water boils at 100 degrees Celsius (212 degrees Fahrenheit).

questions.question: What gas do plants primarily absorb from the air during photosynthesis?

context_docs.text: During photosynthesis, plants absorb carbon dioxide from the air and release oxygen. They use sunlight to convert carbon dioxide and water into glucose.

questions.question: How many planets are in our solar system?

context_docs.text: The solar system has eight recognized planets: Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, and Neptune. Pluto was reclassified as a dwarf planet in 2006.

questions.question: Roughly how fast does light travel in a vacuum?

context_docs.text: The speed of light in a vacuum is approximately 299,792 kilometers per second, often rounded to 300,000 km/s.

questions.question: What is the largest ocean on Earth?

context_docs.text: The Pacific Ocean is the largest and deepest of Earth's five oceans, covering more area than all the land on the planet combined.

questions.question: How many bones does an adult human body typically have?

context_docs.text: An adult human skeleton typically has 206 bones. Babies are born with around 270, some of which fuse together as they grow.
A prime number is a whole number greater than 1 whose only divisors are 1 and itself. 7 is prime; its only divisors are 1 and 7.

questions.question: What is the freezing point of water in Fahrenheit?

context_docs.text: Water freezes at 0 degrees Celsius, which equals 32 degrees Fahrenheit, at standard pressure.
There are seven continents: Africa, Antarctica, Asia, Europe, North America, Oceania (Australia), and South America.
